verdict: PASS — working saturation stands for the stated source scope
scope: 2014 dlp Orléans 2–4-player base rules printed pp12–21; all 20 base Place Tiles pp22–23; components p24; optional Place exclusion and expansions excluded. 2015 publisher p3 used solely for its explicit base-Town-Hall same/separate action cross-reference.
review_method: Read the full assigned authoritative prose, compared it with matching-PDF prose after whitespace/standalone illustration-number normalization, inspected setup/core-action/appendix diagrams, and checked each operative procedure against what prompts request. Extra unsolicited key facts were not credited as mandatory requested coverage. Independently challenged timing, optionality, source-defined outcomes, payment/recovery boundaries and exception interactions.

partial_overlap_is_not_whole_redundancy.reason: Q51 directly asks unique-most award; Q20 directly asks tied-most. Q30 directly asks final-round timing.
Q52 requires stack randomization/orientation/reveal procedure; Q15 requires first-event identity and event timing.
Q20 prompt asks five goods and station/Citizen formula, so its incidental coin-value key text does not make Q53 redundant.
Initial Development Status is directly requested only by Q54; Q13 requests landing/passing thresholds.
Q55 directly requests the explicit Development-only regain exception. Physical-item destinations overlap Q18 as supporting context.
Q56 concerns a player choosing their own Place execution order; Q04 concerns turn rotation and irreversible passing.
Q57 explicitly asks when newly acquired passive substitution begins; categories/inspection and owned-ability scope do not directly ask that timing.
Activation with one and permission to send two do not directly ask the choice to send only one when both can be sent.
The one-good cap and empty-link movement do not directly ask whether available pickup is optional.
Choosing a one-of-two transfer does not itself test separately resolving the remaining occupant in a later same-round action turn.
